routes.description: Establish generic theism through libertarian freedom and a personal cause of the universe, then identify that deity with Christianity through resurrection evidence while answering hiddenness and revelation objections.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if its freedom and cosmological arguments support a personal transcendent God, its historical argument supports divine resurrection, and their conjunction identifies the Christian God despite the principal skeptical objections.

motionBridge.description: Show that a God-supported resurrection of Jesus identifies the independently supported deity as the Christian God.

centralBridges.description: Establish libertarian agency and show why its rational and moral implications require a divine explanation.
Establish a beginning of the universe and infer a timeless, spaceless, immaterial, powerful personal cause.
Establish historical facts concerning Jesus and show that divine resurrection best explains them.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Defend philosophical and historical inference as appropriate methods for realities and events outside experimental science.
Explain limited divine manifestation through God's aim of freely chosen relational trust rather than compelled assent.

routes.description: Withhold belief by challenging libertarian freedom, the personal-cause inference, the resurrection evidence, and the ability of Christian methods and revelation to discriminate their conclusion from alternatives.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the cumulative case lacks reliable support at one or more indispensable bridges or fails to distinguish the Christian God from generic theism and competing religious explanations.

motionBridge.description: Show that the presented evidence and methods do not warrant belief in the specifically Christian God.

centralBridges.description: Challenge evidence for libertarian freedom and its compatibility with divine foreknowledge, creation, planning, and prophecy.
Separate a possible cosmic cause from unsupported claims that it is transcendent, personal, or divine.
Require independently confirmable historical data and comparative support before inferring a divine resurrection.
Test whether reasonable nonbelief and conflicting revelations fit a God who seeks clear human knowledge.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Require a reliable method that selects Christianity rather than producing mutually incompatible religious conclusions.
Require generic theistic considerations to be joined to evidence that uniquely supports Christianity.

sections.title: Libertarian freedom and rational agency
sections.rationale: Libertarian agency supplies an independent pro route to God and also raises a central coherence dispute about rational deliberation, determinism, divine foreknowledge, and providence.

sections.title: The Kalam and the identity of the cosmic cause
sections.rationale: The universe's beginning supports the cumulative case only if the argument can move from a cause to the transcendent personal agent needed by theism.

sections.title: Resurrection evidence and historical inference
sections.rationale: The resurrection is the principal bridge from generic theism to Christianity, making the quality and interpretation of its historical evidence indispensable to the motion.

sections.title: Divine hiddenness and inconsistent revelation
sections.rationale: Reasonable nonbelief and competing revelations test whether observed religious diversity fits the Christian God's alleged desire for relationship, truth, and clear communication.

sections.title: Evidential method and Christian specificity
sections.rationale: The cumulative case must employ reliable methods and explain how generic theistic arguments combine with further evidence to select Christianity over rival conclusions.

chunk-001:c001.proposition: If God exists and raised Jesus from the dead, then the Christian God exists, establishing the cumulative case's governing inference.

chunk-001:c002.proposition: Libertarian human freedom exists, cannot be accommodated by naturalistic determinism, and is therefore best explained by God's existence.

chunk-001:c003.proposition: Determinism would undermine meaningful moral responsibility and rational affirmation because actions and beliefs could not have been otherwise.

chunk-001:c004.proposition: Because everything that begins has a cause and the universe began, its best explanation is a timeless, spaceless, immaterial, powerful mind.

chunk-001:c006.proposition: Prior reason to accept God and Jesus's claimed divine mission raises the antecedent plausibility of God resurrecting Jesus.

chunk-001:c007.proposition: Jesus's crucifixion, reported post-death appearances, and the disciples' costly commitment make divine resurrection the best historical explanation.

chunk-002:c002-08.proposition: General theistic arguments can legitimately support God before resurrection evidence identifies that deity as the Christian God.

chunk-002:c002-09.proposition: Divine hiddenness is weakened because substantial evidence for God already exists and God seeks freely chosen trust and loyalty rather than mere compelled intellectual assent.

chunk-004:c004-04.proposition: The cause of all contiguous physical reality must transcend space, time, and matter, and state-to-event causation further supports an agent with libertarian freedom.

chunk-004:c004-10.proposition: Christian theism can accommodate apparent supernatural activity in other religions and remains falsifiable through demonstrated internal contradiction or strong contrary historical evidence.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: Arguments equally available to many religions cannot establish the specifically Christian God, and skepticism need not assert that no god exists.

chunk-001:c009.proposition: Historical conclusions require comparative background support and may remain uncertain, while an unrestricted divine explanation lacks discriminatory explanatory force.

chunk-002:c002-02.proposition: Religious claims require a method that reliably selects one hypothesis over competing religions rather than reproducing mutually incompatible conclusions.

chunk-002:c002-03.proposition: A God who wants people to know him should generate observable expectations, so pervasive reasonable nonbelief is substantial disconfirming evidence for that God model.

chunk-002:c002-04.proposition: Competing and internally divided revelations undermine Christianity because believers identify errors in rival traditions without applying the same skepticism to their own.

chunk-002:c002-10.proposition: Libertarian freedom is unsupported and conflicts with a creator who knowingly selects a complete universe and whose plan and prophecies fix how events unfold.

chunk-003:c003-01.proposition: The Kalam establishes at most that the universe had a cause, while identifying that cause as a transcendent personal God requires unsupported additional assertions.

chunk-003:c003-03.proposition: The resurrection's proposed minimal facts are not independently confirmable, and scholarly agreement or assessments cannot substitute for the underlying historical data.

chunk-003:c003-09.proposition: Determinism does not prevent a decision-making agent from revising beliefs in response to new information, so rational change does not require libertarian choice.

chunk-004:c004-03.proposition: Even granting that the universe has a cause or explanation, the Kalam argument supplies no justified knowledge about what that cause is.
